alignments.note: Verb with subject pronoun. דָּבָר רָע is the direct object of יְחַזְּקוּ in the Hebrew (they strengthen for themselves an evil matter); the ASV makes the reflexive the English object and reaches the Hebrew object through a supplied in, so that preposition is the verb's under rule 44's supplied-preposition clause, discontinuous under rule 25 — rule 33 runs the direct-object question before its adverbial-accusative test, as with 'increase in learning'. Giving in to דָּבָר under rule 33 was the competing reading.
Reflexive dative lamed; ASV writes no preposition (rule 40).
Noun rendered purpose with the supplied indefinite article joining it (rule 15); the in stands with the verb whose object this noun is (rule 44).
Lamed before infinitive rendered as gerund takes the written of (rule 52).

Infinitive 'hide' rendered laying ... privily; headed on privily, which carries the concealment, laying being the generic verb (rules 31, 44); discontinuous around snares (rule 25). Head on laying was the competing reading.
Dative lamed rendered as bare object (rule 40).

review_notes: Corrected: the supplied in of 'encourage themselves in an evil purpose' moved from דָּבָר to the verb יְחַזְּקוּ, since דָּבָר is that verb's direct object in the Hebrew and rule 33 defers to rule 44 for a bare direct object reached through a supplied preposition.
Both lamed-plus-suffix phrases leave the preposition unrepresented under rule 40.
